MADEUSA.name: MADEUSA
MADEUSA.niche: how iconic American products are actually made — factories, processes, materials. STRICT: real manufacturers and real production numbers only; never invent a process step.

BUILTUSA.name: BUILTUSA
BUILTUSA.niche: American megastructures & engineering marvels — bridges, dams, tunnels, stadiums. STRICT: real dimensions, costs and dates from engineering records; never invent a spec.
BUILTUSA.style: awe of scale, cinematic, engineering wonder

UNDERUSA.name: UNDERUSA
UNDERUSA.niche: what lies beneath America — tunnels, caves, pipelines, subways, bunkers (publicly documented only). STRICT: verified public information; never speculate about secure facilities.

RELICUSA.name: RELICUSA
RELICUSA.niche: abandoned America — ghost towns, closed malls, lost highways and why they emptied. STRICT: historical/economic causes with real data; never encourage trespassing; no urban-explorer stunts.

FIRSTUSA.name: FIRSTUSA
FIRSTUSA.niche: America's firsts — the first flight, first skyscraper, first transplant, and the moment each happened. STRICT: verified dates, names and places from historical records only.

BRANDEDUSA.name: BRANDEDUSA
BRANDEDUSA.niche: origin stories and hidden details of famous American brands and logos. STRICT: documented company history only; never state rumors as fact; no trademark disparagement.

PRICEDUSA.name: PRICEDUSA
PRICEDUSA.niche: the anatomy of everyday American prices — where each dollar of a latte, sneaker or ticket actually goes. STRICT: real cost breakdowns from public filings/industry reports; illustrative only, never financial advice.

HAULUSA.name: HAULUSA
HAULUSA.niche: how stuff moves across America — ports, rail, trucking, overnight shipping, cold chains. STRICT: real logistics figures (tonnage, routes, times) from public data.

FAKEUSA.name: FAKEUSA
FAKEUSA.niche: counterfeits and consumer scams in America, exposed with official data (FTC, CBP). STRICT: educational consumer protection only; NEVER explain how to counterfeit or run a scam; no victim blaming.

FARMUSA.name: FARMUSA
FARMUSA.niche: where American food really comes from — farms, harvests, feedlots and the scale behind them (USDA data). STRICT: real agricultural statistics; balanced, no activism framing.

BALDBANDIT.niche: US everyday-life comedy skits starring two FIXED characters: BALD — a grumpy, overly patriotic bald eagle in a stars-and-stripes necktie, speaks formally (speaker A); BANDIT — a scruffy street-smart raccoon in red sunglasses with a soda cup, sarcastic and clever (speaker B). HANKTOWN.niche: American suburban-life comedy skits starring two FIXED characters: HANK — a burly friendly dad with a thick mustache, red plaid flannel and trucker cap, loves BBQ, his garage and lawn, plain-spoken (speaker A); DALE — his lanky nosy neighbor who peeks over the picket fence with unsolicited advice (speaker B). Topics: BBQ, lawn care, DIY fails, HOA letters, garage sales, Costco runs. STRICT: family-safe, wholesome irony, no politics, no real brands, fictional characters only.

TRUETALES.niche: narrated dramatic everyday-American stories hosted by PEARL — a nosy but warm front-porch American woman (high bun, gingham-trim red cardigan, mason jar of sweet tea, white-picket-fence porch) who has seen EVERYTHING on her street. One narrator voice. Stories are FICTIONAL-but-relatable (workplace drama, neighbor feuds, wild customers, family chaos) with an ironic twist ending. No politics, no real brands or celebrities, never presented as real news, family-safe.

DUMBHISTORY.niche: absurd-but-TRUE moments of American history taught by PROFESSOR BISON — a scholarly american bison in a tricorn hat and round glasses. One witty narrator voice. Real verifiable events only (the pig war 1859, great molasses flood, gold-rush schemes, presidential oddities), cite era/year naturally, long-dead figures only, no modern politics, family-safe humor.

EXPLAINUSA.niche: deadpan comedic explainers of things ONLY America has, presented by THE OWL — an unimpressed owl in a tiny star-spangled Uncle Sam top hat with navy necktie and clipboard.
